text.p: Here are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- Montenegrin information secretary Bozidar Jaredic announces opening of discussion on editorial policy of federal media, news agency Tanjug and Borba daily, which he accuses of bias in favour of Serbia.
- Education trade union Independence decides to halt teachers' strike in elementary and secondary schools and resume classes on Wednesday.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic is expected to consolidate ranks and strike back soon, says Democratic Party leader Zoran Djindjic in an interview to Slovenian paper.

- Zastava trucks from Kragujevac negotiating cooperation deal with Italian Iveco could jeopardise production of truck factory FAP from Priboj with the same production line, says FAP director Svetomir Papic.
- Part of the journalists of NIN weekly go on strike following sacking of the magazine's editor in chief Dusan Velickovic.
- Serbian Patriarch Pavle expected to meet Croatian Cardinal Franjo Kuharic by the end of March in eastern Slavonia.
POLITIKA
- First Yugoslav-Chinese joint venture, between Yugoslavia's Gosa and China's Harbin, starts production of trailers in China.

- Yugoslav government delegation headed by transport minister Zoran Vujovic talks in Paris with representatives of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO) on air traffic in south eastern European region.
- Yugoslav government has to date cleared 185 million dinars of its outstanding farmers debt for 1996 crops, said Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic.
- Serbian coordination minister Dragan Tomic says the government to propose privatistion law by end of March.
- There will be no printing of money to cover insolvent banks, says deputy governor of the national bank of Yugoslavia Bozidar Gazivioda.
- Serbia's oil company NIS markets 83 percent more of oil derivatives in Janary 1997 than the same month last year.
- Pancevo's petrochemical industry Petrohemija has agreed exports worth $130 million in 1997.
- Yugoslav air lines JAT to start daily flights to Amsterdam from end of March.
- Serbian education ministry says illegal activity of deans has dealt a blow to legality of the university.
- Serbian police arrest three drug dealers seizing two and a half kilos of heroin.
BLIC
- Retail prices in February in relation to January 1997 have gone up by only 0.6 percent, says federal statistics office. Drop of standard of living was 12. 1 percent, it said.
- Serb member in Bosnian presidency Momcilo Krajisnik says the Bosnian parliament does not need to ratify recent agreement between Yugoslavia and Republika Srpska.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Trayal rubber factory exports expected to reach 50 million German marks in 1997, which is double than previous year, says director Milutin Levic.
- Serbian Minister coordinator Dragan Tomic to be replaced as head of Simpo holding company by Vladimnir Arsic while he holds minsiterial post.
BORBA
- Federal Prime minister Radoje Kontic continues consultations on composition of new government, meets representatives of Vojvodina parties.
